# Results

**Synthetic data, local in-process simulation (no cluster).** Generated by `canary report`. The effects are planted on purpose: v2-bad
ships v2-good's weights with a feature-order bug and a missing divide-by-zero guard.
Latency is measured inside one Python process, so it only shows the check runs.

## Offline metrics (synthetic test set, 3,000 students, scored through the serving code)

| Model | ROC AUC | Requests that fail (HTTP 500) | Mean predicted risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | 0.838 | 0.0% | 0.315 |
| v2-good | 0.842 | 0.0% | 0.316 |
| v2-bad | 0.798 | 6.1% | 0.503 |

## Canary rollout, window by window

Stable = v1, 10 replicas, 200 requests per side before any decision. Fail if canary error rate > stable + 1%, prediction PSI > 0.2, or p95 latency > 1.5x stable and +25 ms.

## Input and output drift vs the v1 training reference (`canary drift`)

| Feature | PSI, same population | Status | PSI, shifted cohort | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| age_at_enrollment | 0.011 | ok | 0.315 | alert |
| scholarship_holder | 0.001 | ok | 0.040 | ok |
| debtor | 0.000 | ok | 0.086 | ok |
| tuition_up_to_date | 0.000 | ok | 0.021 | ok |
| sem1_enrolled | 0.006 | ok | 0.006 | ok |
| sem1_approved | 0.004 | ok | 0.334 | alert |
| sem1_grade | 0.010 | ok | 0.502 | alert |
| prediction_score | 0.003 | ok | 0.598 | alert |

PSI rule of thumb: < 0.1 ok, 0.1-0.25 warn, > 0.25 alert.
